description:
About the Position

Lund University invites applications for a doctoral student in biomedical engineering specialising in engineering acoustics. The project bridges bioacoustics and medical technology, taking the echolocation abilities of dolphins as inspiration for advances in computational acoustics and medical ultrasound. The doctoral student will model acoustic signal generation and reception, analyse how biological systems solve detection and localisation problems in challenging environments, and translate these insights into improved ultrasound methods.

The position is a salaried four-year doctoral employment within the Faculty of Engineering (LTH) in Lund, a technical environment with strong traditions in acoustics research and biomedical engineering. The work combines computational modelling, signal processing and experimental validation, in collaboration with colleagues across the engineering acoustics and biomedical engineering groups. The unusual interdisciplinary angle of the project makes it attractive for candidates with curiosity-driven research interests and solid quantitative foundations.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in biomedical engineering, electrical engineering, physics or a related field, with strong skills in mathematics, programming and signal processing. Prior exposure to acoustics, ultrasound or bioacoustics is an advantage but not a requirement. Applications are submitted through Lund University's Varbi recruitment portal with a CV, transcripts, references and a personal statement describing the applicant's background and interest in the project.

Highlights

  • Salaried four-year PhD in biomedical engineering at Lund LTH
  • Dolphin echolocation as inspiration for acoustic engineering
  • Computational acoustics and medical ultrasound methods
  • Modelling, signal processing and experimental validation
  • Interdisciplinary bioacoustics-medical technology project
  • Application via the Varbi recruitment system

Lund University, founded in 1666, is one of Sweden's largest and most international universities and a member of the League of European Research Universities. Its faculties cover engineering, science, medicine, economics, humanities, social sciences, law and the performing arts, and the nearby Copenhagen area makes the Oresund region a strong research hub. Doctoral students are salaried employees under Swedish collective agreements, and postdoctoral fellowships are advertised through the university's Varbi recruitment portal. The university ranks among the top 100 research universities worldwide in major rankings.
